samples.summary: Measuring the local file first swallows the server's validation message for image types the browser cannot decode
samples.evidence: `insertImageFromFile` now does `await loadFileDimensions(file)` (line 135) *before* `await upload(file)` (line 136). The docs editor's drop/paste filter accepts anything matching `image/*` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2930-2932`), and `ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` is only png/jpeg/gif/webp (`packages/backend/src/image/image.constants.ts:44`). For a realistic case such as an iPhone `image/heic` drop in Chrome, `loadFileDimensions` rejects with the generic `new Error("Failed to read image")` (line 112) and the upload is never attempted, so the user is toasted "Image upload failed: Failed to read image" instead of the server's `Unsupported file type: image/heic` that the old order produced. Same class for `image/svg+xml` ("Image has zero dimensions", line 107). No data loss, but the refusal reaching the user is now less accurate than the one the backend deliberately shares via `unsupportedFileTypeMessage`.

samples.summary: Dropping the preflight probe of the uploaded URL means an unreachable stored URL is now inserted silently instead of failing loudly
samples.evidence: The previous flow was `url = await uploadImageFile(file); await loadImageDimensions(url)` — the probe doubled as a verification that the URL just stored in the CRDT is actually fetchable. The new flow measures the local blob and inserts `url` unverified (lines 135-142). If the returned URL is wrong or unreadable for the inserting client (e.g. the docs image-URL resolver is not installed on that mount, or the read route refuses), the failure is now silent: `packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts:100-105` caches the failed element and the docs canvas has no `isImageFailed`/placeholder path (unlike slides, `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/image-cache.ts:111`), so the user sees a blank rectangle with no toast and no console error. The trade-off is justified in the comment for the share path, but the loss of the loud failure applies to the owner path too.

samples.summary: `uploadImage` silently falls back to the authenticated (logout-on-401) uploader when `token` is falsy on the shared mount
samples.evidence: `const uploadImage = useMemo(() => (token ? shareTokenImageUploader(token) : undefined), [token])` (lines 331-334). `undefined` makes `insertImageFromFile` fall back to `uploadImageFile` → `docsImageUploader` → `fetchWithAuth`, i.e. exactly the 401 → `logout()` → `redirectTo("/login")` path (`packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:153-161`) that issue #1037 is about. It is unreachable today only because `SharedDocumentByToken` early-returns "No share token provided" when `!token` (shared-document.tsx:1087-1090); `SharedDocsLayout`'s own prop is typed `token?: string`, so nothing local prevents the regression if that upstream guard ever moves. Failing closed (no uploader / an explicit error) would be safer than falling back to the ejecting path.

samples.summary: No disposed/unmounted check between the awaited upload and `editor.insertImage` on the fire-and-forget drop path
samples.evidence: `editor.onImageFileDrop((file, pos) => { void insertImageFromFile(editor, file, pos, uploadImageRef.current); })` captures the editor instance, and `insertImageFromFile` awaits a network round trip before calling `editor.insertImage(url, ...)` (image-insert.ts:136-143). If the visitor navigates away (or the Yorkie doc detaches) while the upload is in flight, `insertImage` runs against a disposed editor — `editor.ts:4315-4331` tears down cursor/textEditor/listeners — and whatever it throws is caught by the blanket handler and reported as "Image upload failed", after the bytes were stored. The bug predates this diff, but the diff owns this async sequence and adds a second awaited step to it.
